text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Rabobank finalises acquisition of 50 pct stake in Robeco investment group; both parties seek expansion abroad. (p1)
- Philips Electronics signs letter of intent to sell its 50 percent stake in cable operator UPS to its U.S. partner United International Holding UIH. (p1)
- Rabobank withdraws its fiscal plans for relaunching defunct aircraft maker Fokker. (p1)
- AEX index reaches yet another record at 750.19. (p1)
- Chemicals concern DSM's 1996 net profit falls, but company is upbeat about this year's prospects. (p1)
- PTT Telecom (KPN) KPN.AS and transmission station company Nozema in talks on joint sales of cable company Casema. (p1)
- Trading company Ceteco targets 10 pct EPS growth. (p5)
- Van der Hoop Effectenbank sees sharply higher 1996 earnings; the bank maintains positive outlook. (p9) DE VOLKSKRANT
- High court rules that employer is responsible for damages to employee's health due to working with dangerous materials. (p1)
- Dutch swine fever emerges in Italy. (p1)
- Food company Nutricia is to drastically restructure its organisation. (p2)
- Consumer confidence in the Netherlands remains high. (p2) DE TELEGRAAF
- Some 40,000 old people in homes for the elderly live in poverty due to rising number of donations they have to make. (p1)
- Realty fund Wereldhave is positive about this year's results. (p23)
- Economic institute for the building trade EIB forecasts both higher turnover and profit for 1997. (p19) TROUW
- European Union decides to investigate the takeover of toy shop chain Toys'R US by retailer Blokker. (p6)
- DSM is interested in taking over Unilever's units Unichema and National Stark. (p7) ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Cabinet is prepared to invest 400 million guilders in restart of Fokker. (p1)
- ABN Amro bank gets listing on Wall Street this May. (p11)
--Amsterdam newsdesk +31-20-504-5000
